summary: The basis revision landed its receipt and the applicability counterevidence is answered from the target's own behaviour. With SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s and MaxAppendEntries 64 left in force and reported as admission operands, both declared comparisons hold and complete: a node with no snapshot yet taken (persisted commit index 10001 above last-applied 0, window 10001 entries, 157 batches) did not return from NewRaft, a node whose newest snapshot sits at index 4002 with 9998 commits above it did not return, and the same snapshot with only 1999 commits above it returned in 7ms. Every non-return sampled a goroutine still inside the replay send (raft.go:1305, raft.go:1346, api.go:753, api.go:606), so the mechanism is the same one already established. The judgment change I recorded: the earlier counterevidence that windows were only obtainable by disabling automatic snapshotting no longer stands, and the registered gap is resolved with a specific basis rather than by assertion — runSnapshots consults shouldSnapshot only on the interval timer, shouldSnapshot is a delta test against the threshold, and the replay window is whatever accumulated from the newest snapshot to the persisted commit index, so with the captured defaults the window exceeds the 8192-entry bound above roughly 68 sustained commits per second, and a sufficiently short SnapshotInterval relative to the write rate keeps it below. I kept that rate premise as a scope-narrowing counterevidence rather than hiding it, and left the standing limits in place (no wall-clock interval elapsed, user-placed snapshot phase, single-voter in-memory setup, unmeasured queue memory, operator recovery untested). The paused TimeoutNow authority lead remains the next open thread; its resume conditions still require a real internal producer prefix for a late or repeated transfer message and a settled safety side.
